title: FlowX Application Manifest
description: Complete machine-readable description of a FlowX application's capability graph. Emitted by FlowX.Compiler as a first-class build artifact (ADR-0005). Structure only — never secrets, never business data; asserted by the ManifestContainsNoSecrets CI test.

schemaVersion.description: SemVer of this schema. Consumers pin a major version.

schemas.description: JSON Schema for every contract type, referenced by $ref from inputs and outputs. Drives OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, MCP tool descriptors and validation from one source.

extensions.description: Custom metadata. Exists so a one-off need never forces a breaking change to this schema.

identity.description: Business identity in <domain>.<verb> form, e.g. inventory.reserve.

sourceRef.description: file:line of the declaration, so every node in the graph is navigable.

profile.description: The cost/reliability trade-off (ADR-0003). Ephemeral is the default.

errors.description: Every error code this flow can produce, aggregated from its capabilities. Generated OpenAPI responses derive from it.

sensitive.description: Members of this contract carrying [Sensitive]. Present only when the contract has at least one, so a contract with no secrets is unchanged by this field existing. Declarative: it records which members carry secrets, and does not itself redact.

trigger.description: One declared way of starting a flow (ADR-0004). Address and admission only — operational tuning such as consumer concurrency, cron jitter or stream checkpoint interval is declared on the same attributes and deliberately absent here, because it configures how the platform runs a trigger rather than what the trigger promises anyone outside it.

description.description: Agent triggers only: the tool description shown to the model.

compensation.description: The business inverse, run in strict reverse order on failure.

fallback.description: The capability a declared Fallback<TCapability>() asks when this step has failed for the last time, as <id>@<version>. Structure, not a value: it names a second dependency this step may invoke, and the capability itself is described in full in the top-level capabilities inventory, exactly as a compensation is. Absent on a step with no fallback and on one whose fallback is a declared constant — a constant is an answer rather than a dependency, and there is nothing for a consumer to resolve.

flow.description: SubFlow steps only: the business identity of the composed flow, matching that flow's own entry. Structure, not a value — it is what makes a set of flow documents a graph a reviewer or an agent can walk. The child's steps are deliberately not inlined; they belong to the child's entry, so one edit to a shared flow is one diff.

mode.description: SubFlow steps only: how the child relates to the parent. Inline shares the parent's correlation and remaining budget, and its failure is the parent's; Detached has its own deadline and lifecycle. AwaitCompletion is absent because it is refused at build time (FLOWX1026) until a journal exists to suspend into.

merge.description: Parallel steps only: how the branches are joined. Structure, not a value — it says what one branch failing means for the flow. A Quorum's size is deliberately absent: it comes from an arbitrary expression in the flow's source, and the manifest carries structure and never values.

signal.description: AwaitSignal steps, and Poll steps that declared .OrSignal<T>(): the identity of a signal that ends this step's wait — the name a transport addresses a delivery to, and the string StepNode.SignalType carries. Structure, not a value: it is the flow's inbound address for being continued, exactly as a trigger is its inbound address for being started. Present on every AwaitSignal step; a step whose contract could not be resolved produces no step at all. On a Poll it is absent unless the author declared a second way for the wait to end, which is the difference a reader should see.

timeout.description: AwaitSignal and Poll steps only: the wait the author declared, evaluated at compile time. On an AwaitSignal it is how long the signal has to arrive; on a Poll it is how long the loop keeps trying, measured from its first attempt. Absent when the declaring expression could not be evaluated — the plan carries the expression verbatim because generated C# can, and a symbol name is not a duration to a reader who has never seen the assembly. Nothing arms this: there is no scheduler and no timer table, so it states what was declared, as the step's policies do.

idempotent.description: Gates whether a retry policy is permitted at all (FLOWX1014).

sideEffects.description: Named external effects. Drives blast-radius analysis and agent confirmation prompts.

partitionKey.description: Ordering is guaranteed per key only — never globally.

stage.description: Fixed by the platform, never configurable (ADR-0011).
